interpretation: Each thing is most such, compared with the others, when the synonymous quality belongs to the others in virtue of it (fire, the cause of heat to the others, is hottest); so what causes the posterior things to be true is most true, the principles of the eternal beings are cause of being to the others, and as each thing stands to being, so to truth. Read for being: what is prior as the cause on which another's being depends is more a being than it. The statement is used with Aquinas' simple priority of ST I q.3 a.1 ('quod est in potentia, non reducitur in actum nisi per ens actu'), read in #166 as dependence of being in act; that identification of Aquinas' 'prior simpliciter' with Aristotle's priority as cause to the posterior is an interpretive step of this claim. It excludes mutual simple priority (result AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-FIRST-MOVER-IS-FIRST-BEING, withoutPriorMoreNotFirstBeing).
